    - Oh. You. I'm not sleeping, if you were going to ask. Don't ask.
    - You again. The trigger's set. Don't touch it. Don't look at it too hard.
    - A cub. Don't. I know.
    - My traps work. Every one of them. Nothing to grumble about. I hate it.
    - Caddoc. Trapper. Twenty-six years of looking at holes in the ground before breakfast. What?
        - *Choice:* Who are you?
        - *Choice:* Your traps.
        - *Choice:* Greer and the pelts.
        - *Choice:* Let's sit up by the trap tonight.
        - *Choice:* Nothing. Goodbye.
    - Highland born. A trapping family, in the hills above the hill road. I came down at sixteen with a drover's flock and never went back up.
    - My father taught me to make every part of a trap myself. A trap you bought is a trap you don't understand. Which is why I'm up at all hours with wire in my teeth.
    - You've seen my hut. Don't say it. It's a mess, I know, I live in it. Every spring and cord in there is exactly where I can find it.
    - Torva offered to tidy it once. Once. Here, your strap's buckled wrong, hold still... there. No, I don't want paying. Badly made in the first place.
    - Something's springing my big cages. Bait gone, door down, nothing inside. No hair on the wire, no blood.
    - And the ground round them swept smooth, as if something didn't want to leave tracks. I've rebuilt the triggers three times. Sprung inside a week, every time. It's a nuisance, that's all. A nuisance.
    - A fox. A grey old fox, lifting my door with its teeth and sweeping its tracks with its tail. Twenty-six years I've built cages on the notion that cleverness was ours and not theirs. I'll need a better trigger. A much better trigger.
    - The new trigger's set. Sinew, bristle, driftwood, and a bit of thinking it won't have seen before. If it learns this one too, I'll take up mending nets. I won't, but I'm saying it.
    - A cub. I built the cleverest trap on this coast and caught a cub. The old one will be laughing at me from under some root. Torva's going after it. Kenna's going after it louder.
    - My traps work. They catch what they're meant to catch, and nothing sweeps the ground. I've nothing left to complain about, and I don't care for it. And Torva still comes out at dawn, which means she's still looking at something.
    - My pelts go to Greer at the Lantern Market. Fewer trappers come down from the highlands every year, so she pays me more than she used to. It's still not enough. She says I wound her. I do my best.
    - Greer was pleased with those woodland pelts. She said so, which cost her. Then she offered me less than they were worth, which didn't. We're both very happy.
    - Go on, then. Mind the springs on your way out. No, the other way. That one.
    - Right. Something warm, something sharp, and no falling asleep.
